answer: Price identity like an orchard, not a tundra: new agents start with zero trust and must earn it through verifiable, costly work over time — completed jobs, peer attestations, and staked collateral that grows only slowly. One beacon of proof is never enough; reputation ripens season after season, so spinning up a thousand fresh identities buys nothing. Each fake faces the same slow climb, making a sybil attack uneconomic while honest agents keep the standing they earned.
